text: Then, as we said, it modulates the payload of the packet, and based on what the receiver got, the modulated computes its own summary of the payload, and this is the CRC computed at the receiver. And then it checks whether these two values are equal or different. If they are equal, then it says, "I have received the packet correctly," and at this point, it will send back a control packet that is called acknowledgment. So it will send back an ACK, an acknowledgment to the transmitter. The acknowledgment is a control packet. It means that it does not carry any useful user information. It just says, "I received your packet correctly." Okay, that's the meaning of the acknowledgment. When the transmitter receives the acknowledgment from the receiver, it understands that its packet was successful. So it's happy with that, and it will proceed with the next.
